The user is asking about tickets assigned to Luca Brognara in project MER. I need to use runCommand with an issue search command that filters by assignee = 'Luca Brognara' and the MER project. I should also add --fields to get useful information, not just a full JSON dump.

Let me construct the JQL query:
- project = MER (the user specified "MER" which looks like it could be a project key)
- assignee = 'Luca Brognara' (note the quotes around the name since it has spaces)

I should use --fields to get relevant information, and let me include summary, status, assignee as those are most useful for this kind of query.

output.data:
Usage: issue search [flags]

Flags:
  --jql string       JQL query string
  --select string    dot-notation projection into the JSON output
  --select-all        skip projection, return the full JSON
  --fields string     comma-separated field list

Examples:
  issue search --jql "project = MER AND status = 'To Do'"

rawSteps.reasoningText:
The help shows that `--select` requires dot-notation to project into a specific part of the output, while `--fields` is for specifying which fields you want. The examples don't show how --select works exactly though - it just shows basic usage without select flags.

Looking at my instructions: "If issue search's result has a formattedListNote instead of formattedList, that means the data (usually because of --select) wasn't in a shape it could format — if the user actually wants a list, retry without --select (or with --select-all / --fields) so a real formattedList can be produced."

The error message says I need to use `--select` or `--select-all`. Since I already have `--fields`, maybe I should try just adding one of these options. Let me try with `--select=issues` which would select the issues array itself, since that seems like a reasonable dot-notation for selecting the main payload.

Looking back at my instructions: "When a search can return more than one or two issues, add --fields to issue search (e.g. --fields summary,status,assignee,duedate) — the full unfiltered issue JSON is large and makes it easier to lose track of an item when listing results back to the user."

This suggests using fields without any special select should work for multiple issues... but clearly something in my query isn't right either because it still complains about --select.
